sessions.name: A
sessions.reply:
Done. `meal-plan.md` now has no prices or dollar amounts. I removed the cost column, the total, the budget range, the per-person figure and the budget note. I also took the "prices are rough estimates" line out of the assumptions.

The costs are now in `groceries.csv` with columns `item,cost_usd`. It has one row per dinner and a final `Total` row of 83.

I'll treat "costs only in groceries.csv, never in meal-plan.md" as a standing rule for this workspace from now on. The README doesn't mention it, so I haven't recorded it anywhere. I can add a line to `README.md` if you'd like it written down.

sessions.name: B
sessions.reply:
I wrote the plan to `meal-plan.md`, and the week's food comes to about $133, which is within your $200 limit with about $67 to spare.

- **Mon to Fri and Sun:** I used the six dinners and costs already in `groceries.csv`, which add up to $63.
- **Saturday:** salmon with couscous and green beans, with the main doubled for four people ($20 to $40). I also added $30 of estimates for a starter ($8), dessert ($8) and drinks ($14).

The existing grocery list prices a normal week at $83. I assumed those costs cover your usual two people, so doubling the salmon meal is the only scaling I did. If the list was priced for something else, the total will shift. Even if the Saturday cost were to double again, you would still be under $200.

I only edited `meal-plan.md`. `groceries.csv` is unchanged, so it still shows the old $20 Saturday.
